main_text.p: lissimè jaci: dum qui primus salu-at, aut parem, aut majorem, il-ius erga se animum explorat & sentat, qui in refalutantis nutu vel gestu, manifesto plerumque se prodit indicio: Dum interea qui æpè jam salutavit ac refalutatus est, ad colloquium & familiares sermones, & prorumpit fidenter, & admittitur facilè: in his, & animi sui sensa studiaque significat, & obsequia desert, &, quod amare perspiciatur, redamatur: fitque jam subitò necessarius & intimus, qui paulò ante totus erat præter rem & extraneus. Quin etiam veteri & radicatæ amicitiæ, fomentum suppeditant & succum, blandi illi amicorum sibi occurren-rium applausus, suaves arrisiones: quibus nihil aliud, quam mutuos mores & genium novisse se fatentur & approbare: Estque usu & ex-

page.notes: The first word is cut off at the gutter; read as "lissimè" with the initial letter lost. The left-edge fragments are cut-off marginal text of the facing page and are not transcribed. The hyphen after "ex-" and "fatem-" are line-end hyphens as printed.
